name.text: Types of Functions — identifying a function family from its graph (JSXGraph)

questiontext.text:
The graph of a function is shown below.

[[jsxgraph width="420px" height="340px"]] var scenario = {#scenario#}; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-5, 8, 5, -8], axis: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false }); var f; if (scenario === 0) { f = board.jc.snippet('0.5*x+1', true, 'x', true); board.create('functiongraph',[f,-5,5],{strokeColor:'#1565c0',strokeWidth:2}); } else if (scenario === 1) { f = board.jc.snippet('0.4*x^2-2', true, 'x', true); board.create('functiongraph',[f,-4.2,4.2],{strokeColor:'#1565c0',strokeWidth:2}); } else if (scenario === 2) { f = board.jc.snippet('0.15*x^3', true, 'x', true); board.create('functiongraph',[f,-4,4],{strokeColor:'#1565c0',strokeWidth:2}); } else { f = board.jc.snippet('2^x-3', true, 'x', true); board.create('functiongraph',[f,-5,3.5],{strokeColor:'#1565c0',strokeWidth:2}); } [[/jsxgraph]]

What type of function does this graph most likely represent?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text: Key visual clues: a straight line is linear; a single symmetric U-shape (one turning point) is quadratic; an S-shaped curve with a turning point and an inflection (up to two turning points) is cubic; a curve that keeps rising (or falling) ever more steeply, flattening out toward a horizontal asymptote on one side, is exponential.

questionnote.text: Grade 11 Functions 16.5 (Types of Functions). Identifies linear, quadratic, cubic, or exponential function families from the shape of a JSXGraph-plotted curve.

falsefeedback.text: Look again at the overall shape: how many turning points does it have, and does it flatten out toward an asymptote anywhere?
